steps.title: Atomic number (proton number)
steps.body: The number of protons in the nucleus of an atom. This identifies the element.

steps.title: Mass number
steps.body: The total number of protons and neutrons in the nucleus of an atom.

steps.title: Isotopes
steps.body: Atoms of the same element that have the same number of protons but a different number of neutrons. They have the same atomic number but different mass numbers.

steps.title: Radioactivity
steps.body: The process by which an unstable nucleus emits radiation to become more stable.

steps.title: Worked example
steps.body: Subatomic particle Relative mass Relative charge Location Proton 1 +1 Nucleus Neutron 1 0 Nucleus Electron Very small (≈ 0.0005) −1 Orbiting the nucleus Key facts: The number of protons = number of electrons in a neutral atom. Proton number = atomic number. Mass number = protons + neutrons. To find neutrons: neutrons = mass number − atomic number . Number of neutrons = mass number − atomic number Worked Example 2: Calculating neutrons Carbon has an atomic number of 6 and a mass number of 12. How many protons, neutrons and electrons does a carbon-12 atom have? Protons = atomic number = 6 Electrons = protons = 6 (neutral atom) Neutrons = mass number − atomic number = 12 − 6 = 6 Worked Example 3: A larger atom Uranium has atomic number 92 and mass number 238. Calculate the number of neutrons. Neutrons = 238 − 92 = 146

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Make sure you can explain all three observations from Rutherford's experiment and the conclusion from each one When calculating neutrons, always do mass number minus atomic number — don't confuse the two Isotopes must have the same proton number but different neutron numbers — both conditions are needed Remember: chemical properties depend on electrons , physical properties depend on mass — this explains why isotopes have the same chemistry but different physics Background radiation is mostly natural — don't forget radon gas as the biggest UK source The plum pudding model was before Rutherford — the nuclear model replaced it based on the scattering evidence
